title: ALU identity and physical package allocation
action: All 90 ALU/Memory symbol instances, including power/spare units, the result buffer and flag-feedback buffer, are assigned to 32 explicit packages. The 49 formerly anonymous instances and fifteen copied-value conflicts are resolved. Unit remapping preserves pin endpoints; KiCad independently checks the resulting net groups.

title: Exact parts and ROM programming
action: FR1/AL2 implement eight SST39SF040-70-4I-NHE PLCC32 devices with private outputs and bank muxes. The runner reconstructs every ALU word from eight programming files; the archived Batronix support list names the exact part and BA005 adapter. Complete physical procurement, socket/passive/footprint selection, programming and full-device readback. AL1's obsolete M27C322-100F1 remains a legacy timing-study reference.

title: Clock phase and loading
action: C1 is a separate KiCad counted-clock candidate: 8 MHz / 8, 375 ns nominal separation, opposite-edge staging, complete-cycle stop and latched single-step. SQ1 adds retained HALT/request arbitration and tests resume/STEP. C1's narrowest internal margin remains 2.30 ns under allocated loads/jitter. Complete debounce/supervisor integration and qualify slew, jitter, PCB capacitance, metastability and receiver reset behavior before replacing the active RC-clock baseline.

title: Non-arithmetic overflow contract
action: V=0 outside signed arithmetic opcodes 3–15. The regenerated ROM matches the independent oracle in all 2,097,152 complete words; controller comparisons include V.

title: Complete instruction and system coverage
action: Extend exhaustive handler checks to every addressing mode, conditional control flow, memory/IO and boundary behaviour; then compare a complete hardware model against the reviewed instruction contract.

title: Controller and full-machine integration
action: Review current FD1/BP1/BL1 results for private DATA routing, distributed clock/reset, logical backplane and CPU-executed ROM loading. Qualify physical loading, flash/ROM programming and readback, supply/reset and the exact oscillator; implement external display hardware. Invalid-opcode fail-stop behaviour for zero-filled unused words remains undefined.

title: Layouts and electrical release review
action: Complete routing; verify pad-net equivalence, ERC/DRC, fanout, decoupling, bus contention, power distribution and signal integrity.

title: Physical calibration
action: Measure clock/data/OE paths on an instrumented prototype and repeat diagnostics at the agreed voltage, temperature and frequency limits.

title: Review migration boundary
action: Native KiCad library import now independently checks pin geometry, aliases, units, rotations/mirrors and hidden supplies. All 1,134 pin groups, including singletons, agree across seven sheets. Source wire/placement/scalar-label parsing remains shared, original annotation graphics are excluded, and fabrication review remains outstanding.

title: Reset threshold and power ramp
action: Manual reset no longer shorts the MCP100 push-pull output; its indicator is separately driven and the settled logic passes. The existing 450 grade can release below 4.75 V. Qualify rail-rise/brownout behavior, supervisor threshold/delay, button debounce and receiver reset recovery/removal. A delay measured from threshold crossing is not necessarily a delay from oscillator-valid supply.

title: Controller peripheral integration
action: SP1/MA1 implement the early MAR transfer with PH1 snapshots and dedicated PC/SP links; ME1 adds protected ROM/SRAM and registered IO. Review the 13-profile candidate results and complete-demo evidence at the IO connector model. Idle-only debounced RESUME, receiver reset and global clock/control loading need qualification.

title: Shared DATA overload and private-link qualification
action: The baseline shared DATA audit remains 90–100 pF before routing and fourteen output pins. FD1 replaces it with continuously driven private sources, mux selection and seven receive branches. Its 324-link audit requires one driver and at most the declared 50 pF allocation per link. Verify actual routing, mating connectors, capacitance over temperature and slew; each 10 pF link allowance covers the entire interconnect.

title: PC shared-bus load and integration
action: PC1 implements four HCT161 counters with falling-edge staged carries and reset-inhibited outputs. Resolve the DATA load: 20 pF of counter inputs plus 50 pF allocated external load exceeds the buffer's 50 pF test condition, before unbounded inactive-output capacitance. Qualify global bus handover, controller timing, reset and PC-to-MAR hold. Candidate simulations at datasheet delays do not close these gaps.

title: Structural circuit wiring
action: The 33 remaining ALU inputs are wired or terminated. Seven sheets now have no findings in the bounded supply/unit/input/direct-family audit. ALU operand and flag storage use common PH3; the disabled old clock buffer has terminated inputs. All previously missing power/spare units are present. This does not establish load, timing or power-integrity qualification.

title: Memory transition timing
action: ME1 models ROM/RAM access, SRAM write cycle/pulse/address/data timing and registered IO. Qualify the SRAM private bus: its 23 pF numeric allocation omits inactive AHCT output capacitance, disable timing is specified at 5 pF and capacitance at 25 C. Reset-interrupted writes, physical address hazards, slew and global bus handover remain open.

title: ALU electrical release and shared loading
action: AL2 retains PH1 result snapshots and synchronous PH3 A/flag capture with FR1 flash. Its isolated shared-DATA stage retains the 90–100 pF receiver budget; the separate FD1 distribution stage uses private links. Qualify actual load, slew, flash startup/readback, supply/reset and PCB skew. The numbered Adam Tech socket alternative requires a separate 1.10 mm-hole footprint; it does not qualify the installed 0.80 mm Assmann-derived footprint.

title: 4 MHz distribution target and physical backplane
action: The bounded FD1 interval review retains 46 paths and explicitly rejects 8 MHz. Source an exact active 4 MHz oscillator, qualify reset assertion/release and brownout behaviour, and complete the BP1 physical backplane. The logical 81-header drawing has no routed layout. Preserve pin numbering and PC1 J1 pin 10 ground strap; measure whole-link capacitance and propagation before physical acceptance.
